**STEP 1 - Scene:** A mixed plated meal with roast chicken, fresh spring rolls, toast and small pieces of cooked meat. It looks like a light lunch or brunch.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** White side plate, about 20 cm diameter. Area = 3.14 × 10² ≈ 314 cm². The other plate at the photo edge is excluded.

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) toast slice, (2) roast chicken drumstick, (3) two fresh spring rolls, (4) two small cooked meat pieces.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Toast ~23%, spring rolls ~17%, drumstick ~12%, meat pieces ~6%. Total covered ≈ 58% of the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Toast ~72 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 108 ml. Drumstick ~38 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 114 ml. Spring rolls ~53 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 133 ml. Meat ~19 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 29 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Using the stated bulk densities would give a toast slice of about 97 g, which is far above a real slice (~30–35 g). I used realistic piece weights instead: toast ~35 g, drumstick ~90 g (bone included), spring rolls ~80 g for two, meat ~50 g for two pieces.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Toast ~270 kcal/100 g → ~95 kcal. Roast drumstick ~190 kcal/100 g → ~171 kcal. Spring rolls ~110 kcal/100 g → ~88 kcal. Cooked meat ~250 kcal/100 g → ~125 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 255 g and ~480 kcal for a partly covered side plate with one drumstick, two spring rolls, one slice of toast and two small meat pieces is plausible.
